correctness.rationale: All i≥1 are handled: when i is a power of two the terminal symbol is new, so the array entry vanishes; otherwise the minimum positive border is d=2^{ν2(i)}, since the suffix of length d equals the prefix exactly while every shorter suffix contains a letter absent from its prefix. For the converse, previous-letter choices at powers of two force a forbidden shorter border; at other indices the known Parikh counts cancel in the mandated length-d border equation and force the unique next symbol. Direct prefix/suffix counting to n=512 and exhaustive restricted-growth generating-word enumeration to n=16 passed; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

evidence: Habib–Shamil–Rahman 2021 Proposition 3.1 and Lemma 3.1 concern binary words; Section 4 provides upper bounds using letter equivalence but explicitly notes higher-alphabet failure of injectivity.
Duval–Lecroq–Lefebvre 2005 studies ordinary border arrays and minimal alphabets using exact word equality; an Abelian border can exist without an exact border.
Fici et al. arXiv:2207.09937, Abelian borders discussion near Theorems 38–40 discusses shortest-border counts, not complete arrays.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Binary rigidity does not imply arbitrary-alphabet rigidity, as the 2021 counterexample confirms. The ordinary border-array minimal-alphabet theorem uses a strictly stronger observation, so even if it covers the same ruler instance for exact borders, it cannot establish that every word sharing only the weaker Abelian data has the same letter partition. The asserted uniform alphabet lower bound therefore is not an implied corollary of those results.

value.rationale: An explicit infinite family of numeric Abelian-border arrays is uniquely reconstructible on arbitrary alphabets despite higher-alphabet ambiguity in general. The exact per-array alphabet threshold produces an unbounded logarithmic worst-case necessary-alphabet lower bound, directly addressing the structural higher-alphabet inverse problem raised by the 2021 source. It is not a mere enumeration of witness letters: all alternative lower-alphabet realizations are ruled out. No global optimality of the lower bound is claimed.
